# Summary of Cairn System Rules

## Pulses
A pulse makes a cairn grow by adding the stride plus a bonus equal to the number of complete stride-sized chunks in the current height. The formula is: new height = current height + stride + floor(current height ÷ stride). Each pulse must be recalculated independently since the height changes after each one.

## Leaks
A leak removes marks after a pulse occurs. It drains marks based on how many complete leak-sized chunks fit into the newly pulsed height. The leak is always applied to the post-pulse height, not the original one.

## Origins (Working Backwards)
To find the original height before pulses were applied, you undo each pulse one at a time by solving backwards. You can't just subtract—you must work through the logic in reverse, testing values to find what height plus stride plus its contained strides equals your known result.

## Drains
A drain removes a fixed number of marks after every pulse cycle. Unlike leaks, drains happen repeatedly over many cycles. The cairn may stabilize at a steady height rather than empty completely, because each pulse can add more marks than the drain removes.

## Merging
When combining two cairns, each contributes a weighted fraction (expressed in tenths) based on shares that sum to one. The merged height is calculated by taking the floor of each weighted contribution, then adding a tether value that's scaled by the shorter cairn's height divided by ten.
